title: FAQ on FAST: How free streaming TV is reshaping the ad market in 2026

facts.fact: EMARKETER forecasts US FAST users will increase 5.8% from 2025 to 2026.
According to a September 2025 Wurl report, monthly active households watching FAST grew 12% year-over-year.
facts.quote: Monthly active households watching FAST grew 12% year-over-year

facts.fact: According to a September 2025 Wurl report, average daily viewing hours per household on FAST climbed 16%.
facts.quote: average daily viewing hours per household climbed 16%

facts.fact: According to a September 2025 Wurl report, average channel session duration on FAST increased 25%.
EMARKETER forecasts Roku Channel, the largest FAST platform, will have 97.3 million US viewers in 2026.
facts.quote: The largest FAST platform with 97.3 million US viewers.

facts.fact: EMARKETER forecasts Tubi, the second-largest FAST platform, will have 92.5 million US viewers in 2026.
facts.quote: The second-largest platform with 92.5 million US viewers.

facts.fact: EMARKETER forecasts Paramount-owned Pluto TV will reach 68.6 million US viewers in 2026.
facts.quote: Paramount-owned Pluto TV reaches 68.6 million viewers.

facts.fact: Per Simon-Kucher data cited by EMARKETER, 42% of paying streamers worldwide think they spend too much on subscriptions.
facts.quote: 42% of paying streamers worldwide think they spend too much on subscriptions

facts.fact: Per Simon-Kucher data cited by EMARKETER, 35% of global subscribers plan to cancel at least one service this year.
facts.quote: 35% of global subscribers plan to cancel at least one service this year

facts.fact: Per Parks Associates, 59% of accounts across the eight leading subscription AVOD providers are on basic ad-supported tiers.
facts.quote: 59% of accounts across the eight leading subscription AVOD providers are on basic ad-supported tiers

facts.fact: Per Nielsen data cited by EMARKETER, adults 18 to 49 spend 63.8% of their TV viewing time with ad-supported content.
facts.quote: Adults 18 to 49 spend 63.8% of their TV viewing time with ad-supported content

facts.fact: Per the same Nielsen data, streaming accounts for 66.7% of the time adults 18 to 49 spend with ad-supported content.
facts.quote: streaming accounts for 66.7% of time spent

facts.fact: Per Gracenote cited by EMARKETER, only 9.2% of CTV advertisers prioritize contextual targeting at the program level.
facts.quote: Only 9.2% of CTV advertisers prioritize contextual targeting at the program level

facts.fact: Per Gracenote cited by EMARKETER, 54% of CTV advertisers say better content metadata would drive more spending.
facts.quote: 54% say better content metadata would drive more spending
